title: Dietary Reference Values for riboflavin
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA), Turck D, Bresson JL, Burlingame B, Dean T, Fairweather-Tait S, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01222).
result: Riboflavin is the integral part of the coenzymes FAD and FMN, cofactors of flavoprotein enzymes; flavokinase phosphorylates free riboflavin to FMN, which FAD synthetase converts to FAD. Glutathione reductase uses FAD, methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) requires FAD, and pyridoxamine phosphate oxidase is FMN-dependent. Signs of riboflavin deficiency (ariboflavinosis) are unspecific: sore throat, hyperaemia and oedema of the pharyngeal and oral mucous membranes, cheilosis, glossitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, angular stomatitis and normochromic normocytic anaemia.
